title: St. John’s Church | Kolkata Trips
description: Explore St. John's Church, one of India's oldest Anglican churches. Learn its history, architecture, timings, how to reach, and nearby attractions.
textContent: St. John’s Church Standing quietly amid the bustling business district of B.B.D. Bagh, St. John’s Church Kolkata is one of the city’s oldest and most historically significant churches. Built during the early years of British rule, it is far more than a place of worship—it is a museum of Kolkata’s colonial past. Completed in 1787, the church has witnessed the transformation of Calcutta from the headquarters of the East India Company into the cultural capital of British India. Today, visitors come not only for its elegant architecture but also to see remarkable monuments, historic graves, priceless paintings, and beautifully maintained gardens. For history lovers, architecture enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone interested in Kolkata’s heritage, St. John’s Church is an essential stop. Quick Information about St. John’s Church Information Details Location Council House Street, B.B.D. Bagh, Kolkata Established 1787 Architectural Style Georgian & Neo-Classical Built By British East India Company Denomination Church of North India (Anglican tradition) Famous For Colonial architecture, Job Charnock Mausoleum, Zoffany painting Ideal Visit Duration 45–90 minutes Photography Generally permitted (subject to local rules) History of St. John’s Church Kolkata Following the Battle of Plassey (1757), the British East India Company consolidated its power in Bengal. As Calcutta expanded rapidly, the growing European population required a larger church than the existing chapels. Construction began in 1784 under the leadership of Reverend William Johnson, chaplain to the East India Company. The church was consecrated in 1787, becoming one of the first major public buildings erected after British dominance in Bengal. The church earned the nickname “The Stone Church” because much of its stone was transported from the ruins of Gaur, the medieval capital of Bengal. For several decades, St. John’s Church served as the principal Anglican cathedral of British Calcutta before the completion of St. Paul’s Cathedral in 1847. Today, it remains one of Kolkata’s most important heritage monuments, preserving invaluable relics from the city’s colonial era. Architecture and Design of St. John’s Church St. John’s Church is an outstanding example of Georgian architecture, inspired by London’s famous St. Martin-in-the-Fields Church. Its design emphasizes elegance rather than excessive ornamentation. Exterior Features Tall Doric columns Classical portico Graceful white façade Beautiful bell tower Large arched windows Symmetrical Georgian proportions The church stands amidst lush gardens, creating a peaceful atmosphere despite being surrounded by Kolkata’s busy commercial district. Interior Features Inside the church, visitors find: High vaulted ceilings Elegant wooden pews Marble flooring Historic memorial plaques Large stained-glass windows Classical altar design Natural light fills the interior, creating a serene environment ideal for quiet reflection. The Famous Painting: “The Last Supper” One of the church’s greatest treasures is “The Last Supper”, painted by the renowned artist Johann Zoffany. Unlike traditional European depictions, Zoffany used residents of colonial Calcutta as models for Christ and the Apostles. This fascinating blend of European religious art with Indian colonial history makes the painting unique in the world. Art historians consider it one of the finest surviving colonial paintings in India. Job Charnock Mausoleum inside St. John’s Church Within the church compound stands the famous Job Charnock Mausoleum. Job Charnock, traditionally regarded as the founder of Calcutta, died in 1692, nearly a century before the church itself was built. His octagonal mausoleum, constructed from stone brought from Gaur, is among the oldest surviving British monuments in Kolkata. Although modern historians debate Charnock’s status as the city’s founder, his tomb remains one of Kolkata’s most visited colonial landmarks. The Black Hole Memorial inside St. John’s Church Another historically significant monument within the church compound is the Black Hole Memorial. Originally erected to commemorate those said to have died in the Black Hole of Calcutta incident of 1756, the memorial has had a complex history and has been relocated over time. Today it stands within the church grounds, serving as an important reminder of one of the most debated events in colonial Indian history. Other Historic Monuments Inside the Compound The church grounds resemble an open-air museum. Visitors can explore memorials dedicated to: Major General Stringer Lawrence Admiral Charles Watson East India Company officials British military officers Colonial administrators Early European residents of Calcutta Each monument tells part of the story of British India. Cemetery and Memorial Garden The beautifully landscaped cemetery contains numerous 18th and 19th-century graves. Unlike modern cemeteries, these monuments feature: Classical sculptures Ornate marble carvings Latin inscriptions Family coats of arms Decorative urns Stone obelisks The peaceful setting makes it one of Kolkata’s most atmospheric heritage sites. Religious Importance of St. John’s Church Although widely known as a heritage monument, St. John’s Church continues to function as an active place of Christian worship. Regular Sunday services and special celebrations are held during: Christmas Easter Good Friday Palm Sunday New Year services Visitors are welcome to attend services while respecting church etiquette. St. John’s Church Timings Church Hours Day Timings Monday – Saturday 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM Sunday Worship services and limited visiting hours Timings may vary on religious holidays or during special church events. Entry Fee Visitor Entry Fee Indian Visitors INR. 10 Foreign Visitors INR. 10 Donations Voluntary and appreciated As entry policies can change, it is advisable to confirm locally before planning your visit. Best Time to Visit The ideal time to visit St. John’s Church is between October and March, when Kolkata enjoys pleasant weather. Morning visits offer: Cooler temperatures Better photography Softer natural light Fewer visitors Peaceful surroundings Avoid visiting during the afternoon in summer due to high temperatures. How to Reach St. John’s Church The church is centrally located in B.B.D. Bagh, making it easily accessible. By Metro The nearest metro stations include: Esplanade Mahakaran (East-West Metro, depending on operational status) Both stations are within walking distance or a short taxi ride. By Taxi Taxis and app-based cabs are readily available throughout Kolkata. By Bus Numerous city buses serve B.B.D. Bagh from all parts of Kolkata. By Ferry Visitors can also arrive via the Howrah–B.B.D. Bagh ferry service, followed by a short walk. Nearby Attractions One of the advantages of visiting St. John’s Church is its proximity to many of Kolkata’s historic landmarks. 1. Raj Bhavan The official residence of the Governor of West Bengal. 2. Writers’ Building A landmark of British administrative history. 3. General Post Office (GPO) Famous for its massive white dome and colonial architecture. 4. B.B.D. Bagh The historic administrative heart of Kolkata. 5. Town Hall One of Kolkata’s finest examples of classical architecture. 6. High Court India’s oldest High Court building after Bombay. 7. St. Andrew’s Church Another beautiful colonial-era church nearby. Visitor Tips Dress modestly, as this is an active place of worship. Maintain silence inside the church. Avoid interrupting religious services. Photography policies may vary; seek permission if unsure. Wear comfortable walking shoes for exploring the church grounds. Carry drinking water, especially during warmer months. Combine your visit with nearby colonial landmarks for a rewarding heritage experience. Why Visit St. John’s Church? St. John’s Church offers a rare opportunity to experience nearly three centuries of Kolkata’s history in one location. From elegant Georgian architecture and priceless colonial art to historic memorials and tranquil gardens, it provides a fascinating insight into the city’s British-era heritage. Whether you are a history enthusiast, architecture lover, photographer, or first-time visitor to Kolkata, St. John’s Church is a destination that deserves a place on your itinerary. Frequently Asked Questions Why is St. John's Church famous? It is famous for being one of Kolkata’s oldest Anglican churches, its Georgian architecture, Job Charnock’s Mausoleum, and Johann Zoffany’s painting The Last Supper. When was St. John's Church built? Construction began in 1784, and the church was consecrated in 1787. Why is it called the "Stone Church"? The nickname comes from the use of stone transported from the ruins of the medieval city of Gaur during its construction. Is there an entry fee? Entry is generally free, though donations are appreciated for maintenance. What are the opening hours? The church is usually open from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with Sunday hours centered around worship services. Who was Job Charnock? Job Charnock was an East India Company official traditionally regarded as the founder of Kolkata, though this interpretation is debated by historians. What is special about The Last Supper painting? Painted by Johann Zoffany, it uniquely depicts biblical figures using people from colonial Calcutta as models. Can visitors take photographs? Photography is generally permitted, but visitors should follow any restrictions in place during their visit. How much time should I spend here? Most visitors spend 45 to 90 minutes exploring the church and its historic grounds. What is the best season to visit? October to March offers the most comfortable weather for sightseeing. Which attractions are nearby? Raj Bhavan, Writers’ Building, General Post Office, Town Hall, High Court, St. Andrew’s Church, Millennium Park, and B.B.D. Bagh are all within easy reach. Is St. John's Church still an active place of worship? Yes.
